walkthrough: Recall that acceleration is the gradient of a velocity-time graph, $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$, so read the slope of the given graph interval by interval.
From 0 to P velocity rises with decreasing slope as drag builds to first terminal velocity, so acceleration is positive and largest at $t = 0$ then falls to zero at P.

From P to Q velocity is constant at first terminal velocity and from R to S velocity is constant at the lower parachute terminal velocity, so the gradient and hence acceleration is zero in both intervals.
From Q to R when the parachute opens velocity falls very steeply to the lower value, so the gradient is negative with large magnitude that then returns to zero at R.
The Q to R change is steeper than the 0 to P change, so the negative peak must be taller than the initial positive peak. This is option B
